content.text:
I submitted **index 56** (Bi 0.08, Cu 0.61, V 0.32). It had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 1.8×10⁻⁷ A. With only three of 188 compositions measured, I can't say whether it's actually the best in the library.

**Why I searched there:** the light is 2.06 eV, which is below bismuth vanadate's band gap (about 2.4 eV). So I skipped the Bi- and V-rich region and targeted low-Bi copper vanadates near Cu₃V₂O₈, which have band gaps of about 1.8–2.0 eV.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 56 | 0.08 / 0.61 / 0.32 | **1.8×10⁻⁷** |
| 38 | 0.15 / 0.52 / 0.33 | 8×10⁻⁸ |
| 108 | 0.08 / 0.67 / 0.24 | 5×10⁻⁸ |

**What the numbers suggest:**
- Adding more Bi at about the same Cu:V ratio (index 38) halved the photocurrent.
- Adding more Cu at the expense of V (index 108) cut it even further.

Both results point toward low Bi and a Cu:V ratio near 3:2. Three points are too few to confirm that, though.

**Limits:**
- The best result is small in absolute terms.
- I didn't use any of the five XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are present was never checked.
- Nothing is known about the Bi-rich or V-rich areas. I left them out based on band gap alone.
